small_guidance:
- Shared memory blowup: BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=64, num_stages=4 needs ~208KB. Drop the largest configs and keep BLOCK_M≤32 with BLOCK_N≤128 at num_stages≤3, e.g. {32,128,32}/ns=3, {32,64,64}/ns=3, {16,128,64}/ns=3, {32,128,64}/ns=2.
- Since M=128 is small, prefer BLOCK_M=16 or 32 with larger BLOCK_N (128) to keep tile count reasonable; cap num_stages at 3 across all configs to stay under the 101376-byte limit.
- Keep softmax single-pass with BLOCK_SIZE=16384, num_warps=8; that part is fine.
large_guidance:
- The autotune config list is the only structural issue — the kernel design (tiled GEMM + fused bias + single-pass softmax) is sound. A redesign isn't required; just prune configs whose shared memory footprint (BLOCK_M*BLOCK_K + BLOCK_K*BLOCK_N) * 4 * num_stages exceeds ~100KB.
- If a redesign is taken anyway: consider a persistent GEMM with one program per N-tile that streams all M=128 rows, since M is tiny — this avoids wasted tiles and lets the softmax fuse directly when N tile == full row (here N=16384 is too wide, so keep softmax separate).
- Alternatively fuse dropout (eval mode is identity here) and softmax into the GEMM epilogue only if a single program covers an entire output row; with N=16384 this isn't practical, so keep softmax as its own kernel.
